pr.title: Star items and show only the starred ones

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_starred.sql adds NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 with CHECK; test/starred.test.js 'AC-1' checks all three seeded items are 0 and that 2 is rejected.
test 'AC-2' asserts exact list with only the starred item marked.
test 'AC-3' stars 3 then 1, asserts only those, in id order.
test 'AC-4' checks / and ?show=all give the full list in id order.

The final spec text (edited after the go in ba6cfe1) says the starred list links "Most items", but src/index.js renders "All items" and the AC-5 test asserts 'All items'. The code and test do not match the spec as written. The States table and core flow still say "All items", so the spec contradicts itself. The edit has no recorded owner decision.
test 'AC-6' checks 400 and no <li> for Starred, none, empty and __proto__. Object.hasOwn guards the lookup.

findings.what: Commit ba6cfe1 ('Follow-up edits', by a bot) changed AC-5 from "All items" to "Most items" after the go. No decision in the spec records the owner's call or a date. The spec now contradicts its own States table and core flow, which say "All items". The code and test still use "All items", so AC-5 as written is unmet.
findings.fix: Revert the AC-5 edit, or if the owner really wants "Most items", record that as a dated decision and update the code, test, States table and core flow to match.

findings.what: The PR body says 'Changed after the go: nothing', but the last commit edits an acceptance item.
findings.fix: Correct the claim to describe the AC-5 edit, or remove the edit.

lenses.note: The spec exists and was read in full. The behaviour matches it except for the AC-5 link wording.
All four States rows have tests. AC-5 was edited after the go with no recorded decision.

Tests assert behaviour and would fail if the code were wrong. I did not run them because vitest with the Workers runtime may not be runnable here, and CI covers that. The traffic fake-app change is a small loosening to carry the query string, and it is justified.
The README mentions ?show=starred. No other stale docs found.
Query handling uses a whitelist via Object.hasOwn; the SQL is built only from fixed view definitions.
Titles are HTML-escaped, the SQL is static, and no instructions were planted in the content.
The diff has no stylesheet or UI framework files; it only adds a link and a star marker to a server-rendered HTML string.
The diff touches no UI files beyond the server-rendered HTML string; no browser flow was available.
The title is within 72 characters. The 'Changed after the go: nothing' claim is false.
